charter.title: What lyrid keeps
charter.lede: The sky is public and works without an account. An account exists to remember three things across your machines, and this page is the whole list — not a summary of one.

noAccount.heading: If you have no account
noAccount.body: Nothing about you is stored on the server. Your marker's shape and colour live in your own browser, and the view you are looking at lives in the address bar. Neither reaches us.

withAccount.heading: If you do
withAccount.addressBody: To sign you in, and to send you a way back if you lose your password. Two letters, ever: one to confirm the address, one to reset a password. No announcements, no newsletter.
withAccount.place: Where you left the sky, and how you like your marked star drawn.
withAccount.placeBody: The reason an account is worth having.
withAccount.sessionsBody: A random token per browser, so signing out actually ends the session rather than waiting for it to expire.

counted.heading: What is counted, and what is not
counted.body: How often each part of lyrid gets used is counted — how many times the radio was opened on a given day, not who opened it. The counters are numbers that go up. There is no row per event, so there is nothing to join back to a person, and no clever query later can turn these into a history of what you looked at.
counted.never: What lyrid does not do: build a profile of your taste, sell or share anything with anyone, run third-party analytics or advertising, or track you across other sites.

whose.heading: Whose sky is it
whose.body: The map itself is built from open data — MusicBrainz, ListenBrainz, Discogs, Wikidata and Wikipedia — and belongs to nobody. Your account holds no part of it.

controls.heading: Your data, in your hands
controls.signedOut: Sign in to take your data back or destroy it.

controls.confirmBody: This removes the account, the profile and every session, right now. It cannot be undone and there is no copy to restore from — download your data first if you want it.

instruments.timeHint: Stars light up in the year their act began. Undated ones stay faint.
